person.name: Alex
person.photo_ignore: its background, its lighting and its clothing

goal: Generate a live-action shot in one take inside a vast abandoned plaza under a burnt-orange dust storm: the camera circles Alex at close range and rises as it goes, until one man standing in the wind has become a figure in an enormous ruined landscape, and the feeling is of someone who has already made a hard decision and is carrying it.
subjects:
The red-and-black striped capsule in @video1 corresponds to Alex, standing alone near the middle of an enormous empty plaza. The grey blocks around the edge are ruined concrete and brick buildings with blown-out windows, the long low steps beside him are cracked stone steps, and the tall dark mass far behind is an abandoned tower block wrapped in dust.
Alex, the person from @image1, wears a long charcoal wool coat with the collar turned up, dark trousers, worn leather boots and a grey scarf; there is orange dust in his hair and beard and on his shoulders, and his face is tired, steady and resolved.
script:
One continuous shot with no cuts, on a 28 mm anamorphic lens, 8 seconds.
It opens at about waist-up height, level with his chest, about three metres from him, looking at him from his left front, with the plaza stretching away behind him. From the first frame the camera arcs around him in a smooth, slow, steady curve of about 120 degrees, passing behind his left shoulder and ending on his right rear, and while it circles it rises: by 3 seconds it is above his head height, by 5 seconds it is well above him looking down at him at about thirty degrees, and by 7 seconds it is about three metres higher than where it started, with the whole ruined plaza and the dust-wrapped tower spread around him. Throughout, the camera keeps aiming at his eyes, so his face stays in the upper third of the frame while the world swings behind him.
Alex: he stands with his weight on both feet while the wind pushes at his coat and scarf. At about 2 seconds he lifts one hand and pulls the scarf down from his mouth to his chin, and looks past the lens at the tower with a long, slow breath, jaw set. At about 5 seconds he lowers his eyes, closes them for a moment, and opens them again with a small decided nod. At about 6.5 seconds he takes one slow step forward into the wind. Orange dust streams across the whole frame, thicker in the distance, with gusts that blow grit along the ground and across the lens now and then.
sound: The sound includes only a low steady wind, grit hitting fabric and stone, the flap of his coat and a distant metallic creak. There is no music of any kind: no score, no song, no singing and no humming, only these natural sounds.
look: a real abandoned plaza in burnt-orange atmospheric dust: terracotta and ochre concrete, black silhouettes of buildings, blowing sand on the steps, low sun hidden behind the dust so the light is soft, hazy and orange.
keep: Keep Alex's identity and clothing, the 120-degree arc from his left front round to his right rear while rising about three metres, the face held in the upper third, the plaza, steps and tower behind him and the orange dust consistent with @video1 and @image2. Keep the lighting and time of day constant from start to end.
place: a vast abandoned plaza in a burnt-orange dust storm. The architecture is ruined brutalist concrete and old brick: long colonnaded halls with deep dark arcades and blown-out window openings on both sides, a tall geometric tower block far away that fades into the dust, wide cracked stone paving drifted with sand, and broad worn steps. Everything is weathered, stained and pitted, and nothing in it is clean. The palette is burnt orange, terracotta, rust and ochre, with the buildings as near-black warm silhouettes that lose their detail with distance. There is no visible sun: it is hidden behind the dust, so the whole sky is one huge, soft, glowing orange light box and every shadow is soft, low and wrapped, never hard. Thick dust fills the air and gets denser with distance, so each layer behind the last is hazier, flatter and more orange; at ground level sand streams across the paving in long thin ribbons and gusts throw grit across the lens. The light is warm, diffuse and slightly glowing, with a soft bloom and gentle halation spreading out from the brightest part of the sky, lifted warm blacks and low contrast, a milky veil over the distance, soft micro-contrast on every surface and fine film grain through the whole image. The feeling is dystopian, quiet and enormous, a landscape that has outlived the people who built it.
